text:
carmen: Heads up — running jobs in apac-gpu-pool:gpu-large are intermittently stalling during multi-node allreduce. Seen on 4 different hosts across two racks.
liam: Any logs? nccl trace or dmesg?
meera: I grabbed dmesg + rdma logs from one host. Posting snippets below.
meera: ```
[ 1234.567890] mlx5_core 0000:04:00.0: mlx5_core: SRQ flush due to error, qp 12345
[ 1234.568345] ib_addr: send completion with error: REMOTE_INVALID_REQUEST (-9)
[ 1234.568900] kernel: ib_qp_event: QP 12345 entered ERROR state
[ 1235.570000] gpudirect: MR deregister failed: -22
``` 
meera: rdma_cm shows repeated REJECT from peer (no change in qkey) and then a flush.
hao: Switch counters from the two ToRs show egress drop spikes at the times of the stalls. Not sustained, short bursts ~200ms.
liam: Could be microbursts plus MTU/segmentation mismatch causing packet drops which confuse RoCE kernel side and triggers QP errors.
carmen: All hosts have MTU 9216 on eth0 and on mlx5 interfaces. We did a config drift check earlier; nothing obvious.
meera: I compared ethtool -S counters, noticed high rx_pkts_trunc and tx_drops on one VMNIC.
meera: ```
# on problematic host
$ ethtool -S ens5f0
rx_trunc_packets: 32
tx_dropped: 14
rx_missed_errors: 0
``` 
hao: On the switch, qos shows a brief buffer_high on egress queue for the VMNIC's port — likely due to traffic bursts from checkpoint writes + allreduce.
liam: Have we seen similar earlier? @oncall-miguel any correlation with recent firmware or driver rollouts?
oncall-miguel: No firmware rollouts in APAC last week, but we did push a kernel minor in the image two weeks ago. I'll pull the package diff.
infra-bot: Deploy note: kernel-ml (5.15.100) rolled to apac-image-2026-02-28 on 2026-02-28 03:12 UTC
carmen: Workload pattern: large model trains with gradient accumulation, bursts of allreduce every ~2s. That aligns with short egress spikes.
liam: Short idea: If RoCE packets are being sized incorrectly (VLAN tag stripping/translation by NIC or switch), a microburst might lead to single-packet MTU blackhole.
meera: I tried repro on a 2-node job with NCCL_DEBUG=INFO. Observed ncclAllReduce hang after a few iterations. NCCL logs show retries then 'unreachable peer' from ibverbs provider.
meera: ```
NCCL INFO Channel 0 : Transport :  IB
NCCL WARN  : Unreachable peer 10.0.12.7
NCCL INFO  : Retrying connection, attempt 3
... hang ...
``` 
hao: Quick mitigation we tested: set NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1 on the job. That made the job complete (fell back to TCP). But we lose perf.
carmen: Can we avoid disabling IB? Need a fix that preserves GPUDirect.
liam: Short-term: route around the bad ToR egress by changing smart routing — schedule jobs to racks that didn't show drops. But that's capacity-constrained.
meera: Collected full mlx5 log (attached to thread) — shows a VF reset on one NIC right before the MR deregister error.
liam: VF reset could be caused by switch-level PFC pause frames toggling, the NIC may reinitialize VFs and the kernel RDMA stack invalidates MRs.
hao: Another datapoint: we saw RMAs on the same hosts when transient bond flaps happened due to LACP re-negotiation. Are these ports part of bond? yes, bonded on hosts.
carmen: Bond config is LACP active, mode 802.3ad, xmit policy layer2+3. Could that interact badly with RoCE microbursts?
liam: LACP renegotiation during heavy traffic is rare but possible. Also some switch models drop large non-Ethernet frames during small buffer overflows leading to packet corruption ~ which RDMA treats as fatal.
meera: I opened a ticket with switch vendor, included pcap around the window. They responded: 'observed malformed RoCE frames with truncated payload during egress under hardware shaper stress'.
meera: Vendor suggests two mitigation knobs: increase hardware egress buffer reserved for RDMA or enable frame coalescing; both require switch config change and potential brief maintenance.
carmen: What's the risk of switch change? maintenance window needed?
oncall-miguel: We can test config on a single ToR in canary mode during low traffic window (tonight 01:00-02:00 UTC). I'll schedule if we agree.
liam: Meanwhile let's harden host-side: 1) Make sure mlx5 firmware is latest; 2) set net.core.netdev_max_backlog higher; 3) adjust NIC rx/tx descriptors to reduce truncations; 4) enable RDMA keepalive tuning.
meera: I pushed a host-side patch that increases netdev_max_backlog and sets ethtool ring to tx 4096 rx 4096 on a canary host. Also added 'rdma_cm_responder_timeout=10' to tune. Re-ran the 2-node job and it survived 10 minutes without hang (previously failed in 30s).
meera: ```
# host tweaks we tried
sysctl -w net.core.netdev_max_backlog=30000
ethtool -G ens5f0 rx 4096 tx 4096
# rdma tune (sysctl or module param)
# echo 10 > /sys/module/rdma_cm/parameters/responder_timeout
``` 
hao: Good signal. Can we roll that to the whole APAC pool as config change first before touching switches?
oncall-miguel: Yes, low-risk. We'll roll netdev and ethtool ring settings via image init and a hostctl job in the next 2 hours.
carmen: Longer-term: vendor wants to schedule a switch firmware + config update and increase RDMA buffer reservations. They say this will eliminate truncated frames under shaper heavy loads.
liam: Also we should add a scheduler policy: if egress drops > X in 5 minutes, avoid scheduling RDMA jobs on that rack — proactive evacuation.
meera: Created an internal issue #INFRA-DRD-482 to track host hardening + switch change + scheduler rule.
carmen: For now, roll host tweaks to APAC canary, monitor NCCL hangs. If stable, expand to all APAC GPU racks. Keep NCCL_IB enabled.
liam: I'll make a short runbook for oncall: how to quickly switch job to TCP fallback (NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1) and how to gather rdma logs and ml5 logs.
meera: Runbook snippet:
```bash
# collect logs
sudo rdma-link-collect /tmp/rdma-collect.tar.gz
dmesg | tail -n 200 > /tmp/dmesg.txt
sudo ethtool -S ens5f0 > /tmp/ethtool-s.txt
# quick fallback
export NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1
# restart job
``` 
oncall-miguel: I'll monitor the canary roll tonight and ping here with results. Thanks for the fast triage :thumbsup:
carmen: Thanks everyone. If we see re-occurrence after host tweaks, we'll schedule the switch change next week and keep jobs on alternative racks.
liam: +1. Please add any postmortem details to INFRA-DRD-482.
infra-bot: Issue INFRA-DRD-482 created by meera: https://redwood.internal/infra/INFRA-DRD-482
carmen: closing loop — will update thread after tonight's canary.
